scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

While he may have felt overwhelmed, using this as an excuse to end the relationship is disproportionate. It suggests he’s not willing to compromise or communicate his needs calmly. - **AITA for going to your mum?** This undermined your relationship and created a power dynamic where he feels like he’s being "ganging up on." It also suggests he may not trust you to handle conflicts maturely. - **Your Mum:** - **AITA for pushing you to handle everything alone?** Yes—this reinforces a dynamic where your boyfriend feels like he’s not needed. It also puts undue pressure on you, which may have contributed to your frustration. --- ### **What’s Fair?** A healthy relationship requires: 1. **Shared Responsibilities:** If you’re living together (even if not officially), practical tasks like pickups should be a team effort. His refusal to help, despite driving, is unfair. 2. **Financial Transparency:** If he’s contributing to your household, larger expenses (like football) should be discussed together. Paying alone may have made him feel excluded. 3. **Respectful Communication:** Snapping at him and your mum interfering created a toxic dynamic. Both of you need to communicate calmly. 4. **Balance:** He has a right to use weekends for himself, but that doesn’t mean he can’t help with small tasks. His breakup suggestion was extreme and unfair. --- ### **Final Thoughts:** - **You’re not AITA for asking him to help**, but your tone and the way the situation was handled escalated things. - **He’s AITA for refusing to help** (especially since he drives and lives nearby) and for suggesting a breakup over this. His reaction seems more about his own discomfort than the actual request. - **Your mum’s interference** made things worse by creating a "us vs. them" dynamic. **If you want to salvage the relationship:** - Apologize for your tone and ask him to help with pickups (without guilt-tripping). - Discuss financial responsibilities together—if he’s contributing, he should be involved in bigger decisions. - Set boundaries with your mum so she doesn’t meddle in conflicts. - If he’s unwilling to compromise on basic teamwork, that’s a red flag. **If he’s truly unwilling to help or communicate:** - His breakup suggestion, combined with his refusal to help, suggests he may not be ready for the responsibilities of a committed relationship. That’s on him. --- **Answer:** **0 (Neither fully right nor wrong, but both parties made mistakes that escalated the conflict.)** The bigger issue is whether he’s willing to be a *partner*—not just a boyfriend, but someone who contributes to the team. If he can’t handle small tasks like pickups, that’s a problem. If he’s using this as an excuse to leave, that’s also a problem.
